correctness.rationale: Qiao et al.'s q-decimal hidden values form a finite alphabet and their finite-precision RoPE is periodic. At a new causal position, each attention contribution is determined by layer, hidden-vector type, and phase modulo the RoPE period. Capping each such multiplicity at 10^(2q)+1 is exact under their softmax convention: a positive type at the cap forces the denominator to Inf and the head output to zero; otherwise every positive multiplicity is known exactly. This gives a deterministic finite prefix state, from which the bounded-halting and ultimate-periodicity conclusions follow.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Qiao et al. arXiv:2609.20335 prove incompleteness for their non-converging Turing-machine class by a repeated-block argument, but the inspected full text does not state a global finite sufficient state, a uniform bound on all halting autoregressive generations, or ultimate periodicity of every non-halting continuation. Jerad et al. arXiv:2608.11909 already characterize a related component-periodic RoPE recognizer class as LTL[P,MOD], so regular single-pass recognition is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. The new claim is restricted to the capped-state theorem in Qiao's arithmetic and its iterative-autoregressive consequences. The source is very recent and residual overlap risk remains.

value.rationale: The result strengthens the finite-precision obstruction from a selected infinite-output class to a structural statement about every autoregressive trajectory in the model: halting reasoning length is uniformly bounded and non-halting reasoning eventually cycles. It also supplies an explicit, though loose, model-dependent state bound.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
